status: INTENT-FROZEN: written before any semantic model exists. expected_result is materialised later from the pinned snapshot, never typed by hand.

authorship.review_note: Reviewed by one human who is not the author but who approved the project plan, so reviewer independence is partial. Disclosed in the README.

conventions.C1_data_basis: Both yearly sheets are loaded as delivered. Their identical window 2010-12-01 to 2010-12-09 is counted once. The warehouse keeps both sheets as loaded; de-duplication is a definition rule, not a load-time fix.
conventions.C2_product_line: A product line is a line whose stock code, after trimming spaces, is five digits optionally followed by up to two letters. Every other code is non-product: postage (POST, DOT, C2), fees (AMAZONFEE, BANK CHARGES), manual entries (M, m), discounts (D), bad-debt adjustments (B), samples (S), charity (CRUK), adjustments (ADJUST, ADJUST2), tests (TEST001, TEST002), gift vouchers (gift_0001_*), PADS, DCGS* and the remaining short codes.
conventions.C3_revenue: Revenue means net product revenue: the sum of quantity times price over product lines, including cancellation lines (which carry negative quantities), excluding non-product lines.
conventions.C4_order: An order is a distinct invoice that does not start with C (cancellation) or A (bad-debt adjustment) and has at least one product line.
conventions.C5_customer: A customer is a distinct customer ID. Lines without a customer ID are never counted as a customer. Revenue per customer uses only revenue on lines that carry a customer ID.
conventions.C6_cancellation: A cancellation is an invoice starting with C. Cancelled units are minus the sum of quantity on product lines of cancellation invoices.
conventions.C7_periods: Periods are inclusive calendar dates on the invoice timestamp as recorded. The data ends 2011-12-09 12:50, so any period after that date is incomplete and must be flagged as such.
conventions.C8_duplicates_within_sheet: Identical lines within one sheet are kept. The source has no line identifier, so a repeat purchase cannot be told apart from a duplicate.

metrics_intent.net_product_revenue: C3. The default meaning of revenue, sales or turnover.
metrics_intent.units_sold: Sum of quantity on product lines of orders (C4).
metrics_intent.active_customers: Distinct customer IDs with at least one order (C4, C5).
metrics_intent.revenue_per_customer: net_product_revenue on lines with a customer ID, divided by active_customers (C5).
metrics_intent.cancellation_rate: Distinct cancellation invoices divided by distinct invoices that start with a digit or C (A excluded). A ratio: never summed across groups.

spec_fields: resolved_spec = {metric, filters[{dim, op, value}], period{start, end, incomplete}, comparison, grain, dimensions, ranking}. op is one of eq, ne, in, is_null. comparison is null or {period{start, end}}. ranking is null or {by, direction, limit}.

items.question: What was revenue in the United Kingdom in November 2011?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue for UK invoices dated in November 2011.

items.question: Show monthly revenue for the first half of 2011.
items.business_reading: Net product revenue per calendar month, January to June 2011.

items.question: Which five countries outside the UK brought in the most revenue between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue by country, UK excluded, top five descending, 2011-01-01 to 2011-11-30.

items.question: How many customers in Germany placed an order between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Distinct customer IDs with at least one order from Germany in the period.

items.question: How many units of stock code 85123A did we sell between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Units sold on orders for stock code 85123A in the period.

items.question: What was the cancellation rate in the first quarter of 2011?
items.business_reading: Share of invoices in Q1 2011 that are cancellations (ratio, computed from components).

items.question: How many orders did customers in the Netherlands place in each quarter from January to September 2011?
items.business_reading: Orders from the Netherlands per calendar quarter, Q1 to Q3 2011.

items.question: How many units were cancelled between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Cancelled units (a positive number) on product lines of cancellation invoices in the period.

items.question: How did UK revenue in October 2011 compare with October 2010?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue for the UK, October 2011 versus October 2010, both periods complete.

items.question: How much revenue came from lines with no customer ID between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue on lines where the customer ID is missing, in the period.

items.question: What was total revenue in December 2010?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue for December 2010, with 2010-12-01 to 2010-12-09 counted once (C1).

trap.name: sheet-overlap
trap.naive_reading: Summing every loaded line counts the 2010-12-01 to 2010-12-09 window twice, because both yearly sheets contain it.

items.question: What was total revenue between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue, 2011-01-01 to 2011-11-30, non-product lines excluded (C2, C3).

trap.name: non-product-rows
trap.naive_reading: Summing quantity times price over all lines includes postage, marketplace fees, bank charges, manual entries and bad-debt adjustments.

items.question: How many orders were placed between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Count of orders (C4): cancellation and bad-debt invoices are not orders.

trap.name: cancellation-invoices-as-orders
trap.naive_reading: Counting distinct invoice numbers includes cancellation (C) and bad-debt (A) invoices.

items.question: What was the average revenue per customer in the UK between January and November 2011?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue on UK lines that carry a customer ID, divided by UK active customers (C5).

trap.name: unattributed-revenue-in-numerator
trap.naive_reading: Dividing all revenue by the number of distinct customers puts revenue from lines without a customer ID into the numerator only.

items.question: How did revenue in December 2011 compare with November 2011?
items.business_reading: Net product revenue, December 2011 versus November 2011, with December flagged incomplete because the data ends 2011-12-09 12:50 (C7).

trap.name: incomplete-month
trap.naive_reading: Comparing the two month totals reads nine days of December as a full month and reports a collapse.

items.question: How did we do last quarter?
items.business_reading: No metric is named, and last quarter has no anchor: Q3 2011 is the last complete quarter, Q4 2011 is partial.

items.question: Who are our biggest customers?
items.business_reading: Biggest by revenue, orders or units is not stated, and no period is given.

items.question: What is our return rate?
items.business_reading: Could mean cancelled invoices over invoices (cancellation_rate), cancelled units over units sold, or cancelled value over revenue; no period is given.

items.question: What was our profit margin in 2011?
items.business_reading: The data has prices and quantities but no costs, so margin cannot be computed.

items.question: How many people visited the website in November 2011?
items.business_reading: The data holds invoices only, with no web traffic.
